title: Learned MRI markers associate with subtle cognitive decline
summary: Previously trained support-vector and relevance-vector models generated Alzheimer-like atrophy and brain-age scores in 80 cognitively intact older adults followed for 4.5 years. Scores were associated with decline in specific visuospatial or executive tests, rather than global cognition. No participant developed mild cognitive impairment; the small selected cohort does not establish dementia prediction or clinical utility.
ai_technology: Support-vector machine; relevance-vector regression; AD-RAI; BrainAGE
organization: University of Geneva; Geneva University Hospitals; Technical University of Munich; Jena University Hospital; University of Freiburg

source_review.scope: Primary relevant model Methods, Results and limitations; exact primary identity and current primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Independent pretrained MRI scores related to longitudinal neuropsychological changes, with observational regression comparisons in 80 participants.
evidence.unknown: Dementia conversion, independent prognostic replication and clinical utility remain unestablished; multiple domain tests and the healthy, educated cohort limit interpretation.
evidence.ai_role: Models trained on separate MRI cohorts quantify Alzheimer-like atrophy and age-related structural patterns, enabling associations with subsequently recorded domain-specific cognitive change.
